items.title: You cannot occupy protest site for all time; what about livelihood of daily wagers? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that protestors cannot perpetually occupy a protest site, adding that such sites can be occupied only for a specified period to allow other groups to use them. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "You cannot occupy a site for all times to come. There are other protesters. Where will the farmers go? Where will the workers go? Where will the trade unions go? Where will the homeless go? Everybody has a right to protest," CJI Kant said. The Court also referred to the losses suffered by daily wagers because of the protests. "There are conflicting claims. The right to protest is also a constitutionally recognised right, as is the right to trade and carry on business. We are not talking about trade merely in terms of commercial establishments. We are talking about the source of livelihood of a daily-wage worker. Where does that person go for their daily bread?," CJI Kant said. items.title: Related Party Transactions: A governance priority for Indian companies
items.summary: In today's interconnected business environment, related party transactions ("RPTs") are a normal and often necessary part of business operations. Companies regularly transact with subsidiaries, associate companies, joint ventures, promoters, directors and key managerial personnel to improve operational efficiency and leverage group synergies. The challenge is not the existence of RPTs, but ensuring that they are conducted transparently, on fair commercial terms, and with appropriate oversight. When managed properly, RPTs can support business objectives. When they are not, they can create conflicts of interest, regulatory concerns and reputational risks. This makes an effective RPT framework a critical component of good corporate governance. Regulatory Framework The regulation of RPTs in India is primarily driven by the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The Companies Act adopts a broad definition of a "related party" and covers directors, their relatives, key managerial personnel, entities in which they hold an interest and companies under common control. items.title: Shopkeepers need not provide free carry bags to customers: Uttarakhand Consumer Commission
items.summary: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that shopkeepers are under no legal obligation to provide free carry bags to customers, particularly when customers voluntarily agree to purchase them after being informed of the charges. [Ramesh Singh Vs Vishal Mega Mart] A Bench of President Kumkum Rani and Member BS Manral dismissed an appeal filed by a customer against Vishal Mega Mart over a charge of ₹18 for a carry bag. The Commission held that charging for a carry bag would not constitute an unfair trade practice when customers were informed of its price and were free to decline the purchase. " It is also well settled that the shopkeeper is under no obligation to supply carry bags and that too, without any cost and there is no law which mandates providing free carry bag to the customer ," the Commission observed in its order of October 30. The dispute arose after the petitioner, Dr. Ramesh Singh Danu, purchased goods worth ₹1,435 from a Vishal Mega Mart outlet in Almora on January 18, 2023. [Union of India Vs BPSL] President Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal and Technical Member Ravindra Chaturvedi held that insolvency resolution and replacement of management did not bar proceedings against those allegedly retaining diverted funds. “ The replacement of the erstwhile management may have brought its control over the company to an end, but it does not, by itself, undo the alleged diversion or remove the prejudice that may have been caused to the company and the public interest, ” the Bench said. The October 30 order dismissed eight applications challenging the maintainability of the government's plea. The applicants included former promoters Sanjay Singal and Aarti Singal, their daughter Priyanka Miglani, associated companies and other individuals. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a show cause notice to the Municipal Commissioner, seeking a response as to why contempt action should not be initiated. The Court also dismissed the commissioner's plea for more time to comply, slapping ₹5 lakh costs and ordering a halt to salary payments. Additionally, CJI Kant questioned whether municipal officers were deliberately avoiding compliance with the Supreme Court's directions. "Does it not show that your officers are colluding? items.title: Supreme Court pulls up Bhupesh Baghel for attempt to delay trial in plea challenging his election
items.summary: The Supreme Court today pulled up former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister and Congress MLA Bhupesh Baghel over attempts to delay the trial of an election petition challenging his 2023 State assembly election victory from the Patan constituency [ Bhupesh Baghel v. Vijay Baghel ]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana proceeded to uphold the Chhattisgarh High Court's dismissal of Baghel's plea to first examine if the election petition filed against him was barred by limitation. The top court also expressed displeasure over the repeated attempts to defer proceedings. "Let the trial proceed. You are delaying as much as possible. You will have a decision," said Justice Mohana. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The dispute stems from the 2023 Chhattisgarh Assembly polls, where Bhupesh Baghel won the Patan seat by securing 95,438 votes against BJP candidate Vijay Baghel’s 75,715 votes. Vijay Baghel filed an election petition alleging that Bhupesh Baghel violated the statutory 48-hour "silence period" under Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by holding a rally/roadshow on November 16, 2023.

Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Mohan Prabhu made the observation while rejecting a husband's contention that his wife was employed at a private company and therefore did not require financial support. " The trial court records show that while addressing the arguments, the learned counsel for the respondent has produced certain photographs, LinkedIn profile and Facebook profile photos, and contended that the petitioner is working " the Court noted. The Court, however, found that the husband had failed to establish his wife's actual earnings. " The learned magistrate rightly held that the documents produced by the learned counsel for the respondent at the time of arguments cannot be relied, " the Court observed. items.summary: Hospital Emergency Scam: साइबर ठगों ने अब ठगी का नया तरीका अपनाया है। कभी बैंक अधिकारी तो कभी परिचित बनकर लोगों को निशाना बनाने वाले जालसाज अब अस्पताल में आपातकालीन स्थिति का बहाना बनाकर भी लोगों की जमा पूंजी हड़प रहे हैं। ऐसा ही मामला कोरबा में एसईसीएल से सेवानिवृत्त एक कर्मचारी के साथ सामने […]
